title: What if the space station fell out of the sky?
lines: The space station is falling.
What if it fell from the sky, and nobody could steer it?
It's almost as long as a football field.
And it weighs as much as three hundred twenty cars.
It orbits at seventeen thousand five hundred miles an hour.
Fast enough to cross the United States in under ten [minutes](minnits).
But even up there, a wisp of air drags on it, so it's always sinking.
Without rocket boosts, the crew would escape in their docked lifeboat capsules.
The air in front of it gets squeezed so hard it glows, hotter than lava.
The giant solar wings [tear](tair) away.
About fifty miles up, the station breaks apart.
Most of it burns up. But for big spacecraft, ten to forty percent can reach the ground.
Here, that could mean tens of tons of metal.
And its path crosses over most of the people on Earth.
In nineteen seventy-nine, the seventy-seven ton Skylab station really did fall.
Pieces landed across Western Australia. Nobody was hurt.
The town of [Esperance](Esspurrunce) fined NASA four hundred dollars for littering.
Thirty years later, an American radio host paid it.
That's why NASA hired [SpaceX](Space X) to build a tug to steer it down, around twenty thirty.
Into the remote South Pacific, near Point Nemo, where the closest people are often astronauts overhead.
Because one day, the space station really will fall.
